newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on platinum firmness.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on platinum firmness.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended higher on Wednesday from New York's previous close, riding on the coattails of firming platinum and palladium prices, bullion traders said.
Bullion ended at US$344.50/345.00 an ounce on Wednesday against New York's US$344.10/40 close on Tuesday.
"It's just been all platinum and palladium," said one dealer.
Platinum and palladium soared to fresh highs on Wednesday on news of a wildcat strike in South Africa, the world's largest platinum producer.
Palladium surged to a high of US$188.00 per ounce compared to a London fixing on Tuesday afternoon of US$177.50.
"The funds got in and had a go, seeing a chance to make money," said one Hong Kong bullion dealer.
"Who wants to stay short (in gold) when platinum and palladium are going up?" another bullion dealer said.
Some traders noted marginal resistance at US$344 but said the trend was upwards.
Physical demand was heard constant.
Local gold ended HK$19 higher at HK$3,191 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to +1.00 from the previous fix at -2.00.
